correctness.rationale: /workspace/replay.py (sketch, Python 3 + SymPy) reconstructs the full projected vector equation, both bilinear identities and the homogeneous next vector. The shift makes the right side H-orthogonal to u; v spans that complement, so the correction is unique iff a−bt²≠0, and is inconsistent otherwise since t≠0 and the residual pairing is nonzero. For H in the distortion band, Hu lies in the disk of radius ε∥u∥ about u, hence its angle differs by at most arcsin ε. In the claimed cone a−bt²>0 by the diagonal bounds, and the maximal polar deviation leaves a positive first coordinate. The two-by-two tangent perturbation in the basis along and perpendicular to u has eigenvalues ±ε and attains the upper slope ratio; for t<0 conjugate by diag(1,−1) to reverse the slope. The resulting F(r)/r increases and is less than one exactly inside ρ, giving a geometric contraction from each starting slope even under arbitrary admissible stepwise changes. At t=0 the correction vanishes; the admissible diagonal metric makes ±ρ inconsistent and iterates finite exterior slopes by −t³/ρ², diverging in magnitude to the other direction. A fixed metric has leading coefficient −c/a, of sharp magnitude τ by the same angular argument, and ε=0 gives the exact cubic. No assumption of invertibility at either spectral shift is used; the conclusion is for this real two-dimensional exact restarted model, not a general eigensolver.
